
An S3-compatible object store (AWS S3, MinIO, Garage, Ceph, ...) is a
good place to publish data for analysts: a bucket per project, a key pair
that reads it and sometimes writes it. `s3pe` is the client: nine verbs
that move R objects and files in and out, with every request signed,
retried on transient failures and verified against the server's
checksum.

This vignette is not evaluated: a store needs an endpoint and
credentials.

## Configuration

Put the endpoint and the key pair in `~/.Renviron` and restart R.
`S3PE_BUCKET` is the bucket used when you do not say which one.

```
S3PE_ENDPOINT=https://s3.example.org
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
S3PE_BUCKET=my-bucket
```

For one session, `use_endpoint()` and `use_bucket()` do the same.
`s3_config()` shows what the package resolved (the secret is never
printed). Every verb takes a `config` argument, so you can also build one
explicitly, for another store or another key:

```{r}
library(s3pe)
s3_config()

cfg <- s3_config(endpoint = "https://s3.other.org", bucket = "archive",
                 access_key = Sys.getenv("ARCHIVE_KEY"),
                 secret_key = Sys.getenv("ARCHIVE_SECRET"))
```

Keys are either relative to the bucket or full `s3://bucket/key` URLs; the
URL wins.

## Reading

`read_s3()` chooses the reader by the key's extension:

```{r}
# JSON -> list
meta <- read_s3("data/manifest.json")
meta$generated_at

# gzipped CSV -> tibble (readr); `...` reaches the reader
sales <- read_s3("series/sales.csv.gz", col_types = "Dncl")

# GeoJSON -> sf, when sf is installed
regions <- read_s3("data/regions.geojson")

# Parquet -> data frame (nanoparquet)
panel <- read_s3("etl/panel.parquet")

# anything else -> raw bytes; or ask for them
png <- read_s3("report/figure1.png")
txt <- read_s3("data/manifest.json", format = "text")
```

A good publisher uploads a manifest last. If `manifest.json` says the
batch is 2026-08, every file of that batch is already there: read it
first and use it as the version of what you cache.

```{r}
cache <- "batch-cache.rds"
meta <- read_s3("data/manifest.json")
if (!file.exists(cache) || readRDS(cache)$generated_at != meta$generated_at) {
  batch <- list(
    generated_at = meta$generated_at,
    series = read_s3("data/series.json"),
    ranking = read_s3("data/ranking.json")
  )
  saveRDS(batch, cache)
}
```

## Writing

`write_s3()` is the reverse: the extension decides the format and the
content type.

```{r}
write_s3(panel, "report/panel.parquet")
write_s3(panel, "report/panel.csv.gz")
write_s3(list(generated_at = Sys.time(), rows = nrow(panel)),
         "report/manifest.json", pretty = TRUE)
write_s3(model, "report/model.rds")
write_s3(c("# Report", "", "Text..."), "report/README.md")
```

Upload the data first, the manifest last: readers that follow the
convention above will then never see a half-written batch.

## Files

`upload_s3()` and `download_s3()` move files without reading them into R.
A key ending in `/` gets the file's name appended; downloads are written
to a `.s3pe-part` file and renamed when complete and verified.

```{r}
upload_s3("output/figure1.png", "report/")
download_s3("data/regions.geojson", "data/regions.geojson", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## The rest of the bucket

```{r}
list_s3("data/")                   # tibble: key, size, last_modified, etag
head_s3("data/manifest.json")      # one row, or NULL
exists_s3("data/manifest.json")    # TRUE/FALSE
delete_s3("report/draft.csv")
buckets_s3()
```

## When things go wrong

Every failure is an error with a class, so a pipeline stops by default
and you can catch exactly what you expect:

```{r}
meta <- tryCatch(
  read_s3("data/manifest.json"),
  s3pe_error_not_found = function(e) NULL
)
```

- `s3pe_error_config`: no endpoint, no credentials, no bucket.
- `s3pe_error_not_found` (404), `s3pe_error_access` (403),
  `s3pe_error_http` (other statuses, with `$status` and `$code`).
- `s3pe_error_transport`: the server could not be reached, after three
  attempts with a 1 s and a 2 s pause.
- `s3pe_error_integrity`: the bytes that arrived are not the bytes that
  were sent.

Transfers print one line each (`↑ s3://my-bucket/report/panel.parquet
(12.3 MB, 0.8 s)`); silence them with `options(s3pe.quiet = TRUE)` or
`S3PE_QUIET=1`.

## A local store

Inside the machine that hosts the store, or against a MinIO or Garage
started for development, point the session at it:

```{r}
use_endpoint("http://127.0.0.1:9000")
```

## Other editions

The same verbs exist in Python (`pip install s3pe`), Rust
(`cargo install s3pe`, with the `s3pe` command line) and Go
(`go get github.com/StrategicProjects/s3pe`). They share one
specification and one test vector, so a key written by one is read by
the others.
